scope: Existing 41 principal test families. Grouped, not exhaustive of every prediction or later Version 4 result. Earlier draft publication-route codes have been omitted; the current publication spine is in research/UHL.md.

entries.title: H1: useful certification
entries.status: Open engineering hypothesis
entries.next_test: Compare proposer-plus-kernel with strong retrieval, tool-use and fail-closed systems on one frozen, versioned workload. Match evidence access and report coverage, assertion errors, external falsity, binding and trusted-core cost.
entries.success_means: An auditable authority path supplies useful performance within that jurisdiction. It is more than abstaining from everything.
entries.failure_means: Inferior useful coverage at comparable cost fails this implementation/workload claim. It does not refute every possible small-kernel architecture.

entries.title: H2: proposer-size saturation
entries.status: Open engineering hypothesis
entries.next_test: Cross several proposer capacities with the same evidence, binder, verifier, workloads and resource accounting; predefine a practical saturation margin.
entries.success_means: For this workload, generating certifiable proposals needs less model capacity than the comparator. Total cost must include evidence and maintenance.
entries.failure_means: Material continued gains over the declared size range reject the tested saturation claim; certification can remain useful.

entries.title: Memory that preserves future task distinctions
entries.status: Finite counterexample established; utility untested
entries.next_test: Test summary compression with new queries sensitive to versions, entities, permissions and unresolved commitments; compare strong retrieval and structured-memory baselines.
entries.success_means: The retained representation better supports the declared future task family per unit of storage or cost.
entries.failure_means: No gain or failures on held-out queries narrow the memory contract; a single demonstration is not a general state verifier.

entries.title: Recursive action-sufficient state
entries.status: New proposed research problem, extending the static result
entries.next_test: Construct finite action codes and test whether updates can be computed from code, admitted action and observed record alone; compare existing abstraction and partially observed-control methods.
entries.success_means: A compact action code can support repeated operation, rather than only one static selection.
entries.failure_means: Inconsistent successor codes show the compression needs refinement or history. A smaller static cover does not establish a smaller recursive controller.

entries.title: Matched-present state failure and recovery
entries.status: Prospective endogenous-biological test; synthetic and designed examples available
entries.next_test: Match histories on a frozen measurement, apply common futures, bound matching error and discrepancy, then test an augmented representation on untouched histories and batches.
entries.success_means: The original representation loses useful predictive information and the tested addition recovers some or all of the declared predictive scope.
entries.failure_means: Equivalence supports adequacy within the panel; unresolved data do not. Failure of augmentation rejects that proposed repair.

entries.title: A physical carrier of the retained distinction
entries.status: Prospective causal test
entries.next_test: Use lineage-linked state/outcome data and an independently characterized intervention on a candidate carrier, with target engagement, off-target and controller-writing controls.
entries.success_means: Evidence supports a causal contribution of the candidate carrier within the intervention assumptions.
entries.failure_means: Predictive gain without selective causal evidence supports a marker, not necessarily the claimed memory mechanism.

entries.title: Holding effort, reserve and release
entries.status: New proposed identifiability and assay problem from the programme backlog
entries.next_test: Specify a balance model and actual actuator. Determine which calibrated challenges distinguish production, consumption, maximum capacity and controller response. A holding flux alone measures only net imbalance.
entries.success_means: A minimally sufficient probe panel exposes reserve information beyond the steady concentration and net holding effort.
entries.failure_means: Observationally equivalent mechanisms require more measurements or a narrower claim; a named reserve score is not a solution by itself.

entries.title: Restoration after support ends
entries.status: Prospective operational test
entries.next_test: Measure future-response equivalence and persistence after a defined withdrawal and rechallenge; distinguish temporary compensation from recovered capacity.
entries.success_means: Recovery is supported for specified futures, duration and disturbances after removal of the named support.
entries.failure_means: Restored snapshots with failed rechallenge do not establish restoration; success under one support policy need not transfer.

entries.title: Action-relevant distinctions
entries.status: Exact finite characterization; empirical action library absent
entries.next_test: Estimate a finite state-action success table with simultaneous bounds; test common-action intersections including higher-order conflicts, then evaluate a frozen code on held-out units.
entries.success_means: The measured distinction changes acceptable choices, or demonstrates that a cheaper common action suffices.
entries.failure_means: An empty conservative confidence-set intersection is failure to certify, not proof that no acceptable action exists.

entries.title: Safe diagnosis before rescue closes
entries.status: Prospective complete-policy test
entries.next_test: Compare diagnostic-and-action policies including their delay, measurement disturbance and outcome risk. Use the one-shot total-variation bound only under its stated non-disturbing assumptions.
entries.success_means: Obtaining a particular distinction improves operational recovery before the opportunity expires.
entries.failure_means: Prediction without net policy benefit does not justify the diagnostic. One failed diagnostic does not prove all safe diagnosis impossible.

entries.title: Finite-section fold passage
entries.status: Conditional mathematical law; biological hypothesis unvalidated
entries.next_test: Pilot-calibrate the depth axis, then freeze rescue, finite-section family and observation model. Compare fold, cumulative-exposure, fixed-power and hazard models on held-out forcing depths with the same likelihood.
entries.success_means: The constrained passage family predicts an operation-specific recoverability boundary and durable fate in the tested regime.
entries.failure_means: Failure rejects that operational fold model; asymmetric sections need not have a monotone exponent profile, and population T50 is not automatically deterministic passage.

entries.title: Supply-limited oxidative collapse
entries.status: Model calibrated from literature; broader transport unvalidated
entries.next_test: Independently measure supply, demand and regeneration parameters, predict new challenge thresholds and test the threshold ordering without fitting the target outcomes.
entries.success_means: The calibrated capacity-versus-demand model predicts a new system or preparation.
entries.failure_means: Incorrect thresholds within a calibrated regime reject that model/transport; known contraindication recovery alone is not prospective validation.

entries.title: Reductive fade and the surveillance bridge
entries.status: Mechanistic extrapolation and conditional oncology forecast
entries.next_test: Measure the proposed flux-to-surveillance mapping in the relevant cell type, with tumour and normal-system endpoints; establish whether the proposed biomarker reflects the needed quantity.
entries.success_means: A directly calibrated bridge supports the proposed surveillance mechanism and motivates testing downstream outcome forecasts.
entries.failure_means: A different mapping or systemic/tumour conflict weakens the forecast; a clinical hazard-ratio magnitude is not validated by the existing model.

entries.title: P13: controller bandwidth versus load reduction
entries.status: Prospective role-specific intervention prediction
entries.next_test: First demonstrate kinetic-mismatch failure; independently quantify whether an intervention changes controller speed rather than simply its setpoint/capacity. Compare matched load reduction on a declared outcome.
entries.success_means: Changing the measured control timescale improves the relevant pulse-stress outcome beyond the comparator.
entries.failure_means: No differential benefit after verified target engagement rejects the tested P13 instance; faster or more abundant NRF2 are not interchangeable measurements.

entries.title: P14: pinning versus surveillance failure
entries.status: Prospective diagnostic and prevalence hypotheses
entries.next_test: Measure capacity response to a controlled signal perturbation in appropriately stratified systems. Test the proposed pinned signature and the separate claim that it predominates.
entries.success_means: Response dynamics distinguish an upstream pinned controller from the competing surveillance explanation.
entries.failure_means: Normal capacity responsiveness in the claimed pinned class rejects that classification or prevalence claim; population correlations alone can mislead.

entries.title: P15–P17: sensing versus calibration
entries.status: Prospective; calibration and selective interventions not established
entries.next_test: Characterize compartmental measurements, sensor-restoration and controller-targeted interventions independently; test a locked response signature and any proposed fitness/setpoint relation.
entries.success_means: Different faults that yield similar visible readouts are separated by verified intervention responses.
entries.failure_means: An ineffective senolytic alone cannot prove controller miscalibration: inadequate engagement, another fault or irreversible damage remain alternatives.

entries.title: Biphasic shape, peak location and width
entries.status: Conditional model; retrospective support; quantitative prospective tests remain
entries.next_test: Measure activation, damage and capacity independently in one system; predict untouched full curves and check location, width and amplitude separately.
entries.success_means: Mechanistic parameters predict the conditional adaptive curve without fitting those outcome curves.
entries.failure_means: Incorrect predictions reject the specified adaptive model or approximation, not the existence of hormesis. The approximate 2× activation-dose peak is not universal.

entries.title: Control-weighted molecular-to-functional transmission
entries.status: First-order model and prospective same-system test
entries.next_test: Measure control coefficients and elasticities, then predict transmitted adaptation. Include mixed-sign targets and shared bottlenecks; test finite-induction approximation error.
entries.success_means: Control-weighted induction outperforms molecular abundance or target count as an amplitude predictor.
entries.failure_means: Failure within the valid perturbative regime rejects the proposed transmission application; a local coefficient cannot automatically predict a large finite change.

entries.title: Conditional baseline compression
entries.status: Prospective small-perturbation coordinate prediction
entries.next_test: Hold network transmission and induction approximately fixed while varying baseline. Test the stated amplitude ratio based on 1−x0² against alternatives.
entries.success_means: The bounded-observation factor predicts baseline-dependent attenuation within the controlled regime.
entries.failure_means: A baseline shift that also changes network control is confounded; a valid controlled failure rejects the tested observation model.

entries.title: Acute–chronic amplitude split
entries.status: Prospective; overlaps extension P5 and architecture P11
entries.next_test: Declare matched exposure, endpoint and timescales; measure controller response and compare a frozen acute–chronic contrast with a system-justified margin.
entries.success_means: The predicted timing-dependent adaptive response is supported in that system.
entries.failure_means: Adequately resolved equivalence or opposite direction rejects the scoped contrast; overlapping papers are one prediction family.

entries.title: Adaptation as improved later capability
entries.status: New integrative experimental proposal
entries.next_test: After conditioning and withdrawal, test whether predicted adaptation improves an independent later challenge outcome and how reserve changes the beneficial/harmful boundary.
entries.success_means: A transient adaptive signal predicts a lasting, task-specific gain in capacity.
entries.failure_means: A higher acute endpoint without later benefit does not establish durable adaptive improvement.

entries.title: Reversal and state recovery
entries.status: Exact order-blind null; independent published order effects; recovery prospective
entries.next_test: Qualify timing and an endpoint-specific reversed pair. After a resolved split, link prechallenge state and future outcome in the same inferential unit and test held-out recovery.
entries.success_means: A biological representation improves on equal BED for that endpoint and preparation.
entries.failure_means: No resolved split can be equivalence or insufficient precision; a split alone does not identify dimension or mechanism.

entries.title: Gap spectroscopy versus quadratic degeneracy
entries.status: Conditional theorem; experimental implication unvalidated
entries.next_test: Use a qualified gap ladder and multiple priming strengths, with recovery/heterogeneity controls, to test waiting-semigroup closure. More challenge amplitudes alone can be uninformative in the quadratic branch.
entries.success_means: Gap response exposes predictive recovery modes hidden by an acute curve.
entries.failure_means: Failure of a scalar waiting model demands a revised recovery representation; it is not automatic evidence for a named molecular mechanism.

entries.title: Projective observation fingerprint
entries.status: Conditional classical structure; synthetic test; prospective physical branch
entries.next_test: Earn an adequate state and deterministic point-map regime, then test cross-ratios on held-out separated quadruples. Independently examine any proposed physical homogeneous channels.
entries.success_means: The tested operation admits the projective description; a physical lift needs separate evidence.
entries.failure_means: Cross-ratio failure rejects the tested one-dimensional projective branch, not the broader state-discovery programme.

entries.title: Flat/curved defect classification
entries.status: Axiom-conditional mathematics and synthetic tomography
entries.next_test: Independently review the full proof and query an admitted composition oracle across radius shells; control angle noise and test the stated defect assumptions.
entries.success_means: A particular system occupies the classified branch with an estimated geometric parameter.
entries.failure_means: An out-of-class defect rejects applying the classification; it does not justify a universal boundedness geometry.

entries.title: Mechanism-selected combination baselines
entries.status: Exact scoped formulas; assay identification remains empirical
entries.next_test: Use correct single-agent doses and prespecified mechanisms, including the common-shape n=1 contrast if appropriate; compare with full specialist null models under the actual noise model.
entries.success_means: A specific lawful reference improves combination interpretation and experimental discrimination.
entries.failure_means: The maximal raw gap near 0.618 is not a universal information optimum; a failed reference may require another scalar model rather than hidden state.

entries.title: Aluminium/SOD chemical testbed
entries.status: Conditional chemical model
entries.next_test: Establish chemical speciation, relevant competition kinetics, compartment and exposure before predicting unused interventions.
entries.success_means: The named chemical/compositional model predicts that assay.
entries.failure_means: Failure rejects the chemical model in scope; it does not refute the classical additive-generator representation theorem.

entries.title: Frozen prime gap-word prediction
entries.status: Exact identities plus finite computations; probability assumptions explicit
entries.next_test: Independent implementation/enumeration on untouched intervals; preserve positivity/consistency assumptions, covariance and numerical error; compare established prime heuristics and fitted controls.
entries.success_means: The finite predictor transports beyond its construction interval and implementation.
entries.failure_means: Systematic residuals reject the tested approximation or finite predictor; large in-sample R² is not an asymptotic theorem.

entries.title: Resolution versus residual floor
entries.status: Alternative hypotheses, not two predictions expected to hold together
entries.next_test: Compare sparse-aware lifted models across feasible wheels, higher-order contexts and held-out scales.
entries.success_means: Either closure or a persistent resolved finite-scale residual locates what the current representation misses.
entries.failure_means: Sparse high-resolution fits cannot establish a positive floor; finite stabilization does not prove an asymptotic limit.

entries.title: Currents invisible to abundance histograms
entries.status: Conditional non-identifiability; field diagnostic needs validation
entries.next_test: Use labelled temporal community data and held-out prediction; control environmental forcing, nonstationarity, multiplicative noise, exchangeable dynamics and extinctions.
entries.success_means: Temporal structure supplies information absent from the stationary abundance distribution.
entries.failure_means: Irreversibility alone is not unique evidence of species-specific niche dynamics; lack of power is unresolved.

entries.title: Sample the dominance-sensitive trajectory region
entries.status: Exact coefficient result and simulations
entries.next_test: Compare boundary-local and wider-frequency designs using realistic drift-aware inference, equal acquisition budgets and observed response magnitude.
entries.success_means: The theory identifies a practically better sampling design for separating selection strength and dominance.
entries.failure_means: No practical gain in the tested regime limits the design claim; algebraic identifiability alone is not finite-data accuracy.

entries.title: Covariance versus intervention-response rank
entries.status: Model-specific theorem and simulations; no decisive transfer dataset
entries.next_test: Acquire a randomized multi-intervention/task transfer matrix with target engagement, task-specific channels, duration and signal-to-noise controls.
entries.success_means: The intervention family exposes multiple accessible response directions despite a low-dimensional descriptive factor.
entries.failure_means: A failed indirect training intervention does not disprove an inaccessible common cause; rank is design- and timescale-relative.

entries.title: c-ring constraint binding versus slack
entries.status: Hypothesis and retrospective-analysis framework
entries.next_test: Use engineered/within-lineage comparisons with independently bounded environmental demand and losses; test the demand-by-coupling interaction.
entries.success_means: Coupling contributes more predictively near a demonstrated energetic boundary.
entries.failure_means: Confounding by phylogeny, unbounded losses or no interaction weakens the proposed explanation.

entries.title: A discriminating multi-face retention boundary
entries.status: Current data do not identify exponent/mechanism; extension proposed
entries.next_test: Add a coefficient-locked competing loss face, independent masses and suitable exposure/age information; compare forward models and negative controls.
entries.success_means: Data begin separating physical retention models rather than merely permitting a constrained classifier.
entries.failure_means: Equivalent fits among many coefficients remain non-identification; fitting the valley is not identifying its cause.

entries.title: Return dynamics add predictive information
entries.status: Offline implementation; prospective real-signal test
entries.next_test: Predict an independent later outcome from frozen return features; compare static features, dynamic history baselines and matched feature counts with person/session holdouts.
entries.success_means: Return dynamics earn a role in measuring the declared recovery task.
entries.failure_means: No incremental value rejects the tested read-side input; prediction of a score defined from those same features is circular.

entries.title: Adaptive feedback earns a control advantage
entries.status: Prospective intervention hypothesis
entries.next_test: After input validation, compare capped adaptive feedback with appropriately matched open-loop/replay, sham and well-tuned conventional feedback; measure independent outcome and exposure.
entries.success_means: The measured return state improves a complete control policy, then durability and transport can be tested.
entries.failure_means: No advantage rejects this controller implementation/task claim even if the metrics remain useful.

entries.title: Bounded adaptive-world contracts
entries.status: Synthetic controller validation; live estimation/benefit unvalidated
entries.next_test: Validate state estimation and actuator meaning, then compare boundary recovery and user-relevant outcomes with strong bounded controllers at matched tuning effort.
entries.success_means: Typed interfaces improve a real adaptive environment within a stated contract.
entries.failure_means: No benefit beyond ordinary constraints or unreliable state estimation limits the practical architecture.

entries.title: Gamma bridge and dyadic sinh coupling
entries.status: Separate postulated physiological and coupling hypotheses
entries.next_test: Test the single-agent bridge against behavioural belief measures and artefacts first; if supported, compare independently calibrated dyadic sinh, linear, polynomial and saturating alternatives.
entries.success_means: The particular neural/interaction bridge gains support; the coordinate result itself does not establish it.
entries.failure_means: Bridge failure blocks the EEG interpretation; coupling failure rejects that potential without invalidating Bayesian log-odds.

entries.title: Capture–policy–host ordering
entries.status: Hypothesis; no new empirical outcomes
entries.next_test: Predefine capture before outcomes; use blinded coding and prospective temporal sampling with treatment, common-driver, delayed-feedback and non-recovery controls.
entries.success_means: The specified threshold-local sequence adds predictive explanation beyond the alternatives.
entries.failure_means: Retrospective narratives or generic support effects do not validate the ordering; no clinical efficacy or belief-based cure follows.

entries.title: Quantum archive channel history
entries.status: Fixed-archive reanalysis; new archive/physical-time validation absent
entries.next_test: Acquire timestamps and calibration/batching metadata and fit full-count models on independent archives; compare drift, heterogeneity and exchangeability explanations.
entries.success_means: The archive needs a richer channel-state representation for the intended inference.
entries.failure_means: A job-index residual is not a physical time constant, Born-rule anomaly or evidence of microscopic memory.

entries.title: Match the evidence to the imposed intervention
entries.status: Review and normative argument; not a natural-law prediction
entries.next_test: Maintain an up-to-date comparison of the actual coercive intervention with supported voluntary care and patient-centred outcomes; keep the ethical premise explicit.
entries.success_means: Direct evidence can address the incremental intervention that requires justification.
entries.failure_means: Evidence about drug efficacy alone does not settle the effect of legal force. This synthesis supplies no new treatment or policy outcome.
